JMV05.cite: D. Jao, S. D. Miller, R. Venkatesan, Do all elliptic curves of the same order have the same difficulty of discrete log?, ASIACRYPT 2005, LNCS 3788, pp. 21-40; arXiv math/0411378v3

results.Thm 1.1: GRH: on each level, the graph of horizontal isogenies of prime degree <= m = poly(log q) is an expander; random walks of polylog(q) steps hit any subset of size h with prob >= h/(2|G|)
results.Cor 1.2: GRH: an algorithm solving dlog on a fixed positive proportion of curves in a level solves dlog on any curve in that same level with polylog(q) expected queries
results.sec 2.1: edges are isogenies of prime degree < (log q)^(2+delta); valid only when restricted to a single level
results.Thm 2.1(5): if a prime l divides one of [O_K:End(E)], [O_K:End(E')] but not the other, every F_q-isogeny E->E' has degree divisible by l (proof: Kohel sec 4.2)
results.Thm 2.2: counts: l not dividing c_E: 1+(D/l) horizontal, plus l-(D/l) down if l | c_pi; l | c_E: one up, plus l down if l | c_pi/c_E
results.sec 1.1: levels whose conductors differ by polynomially smooth amounts can be bridged in polynomial time; 'no polynomial time algorithm is known which even produces a pair of curves lying on levels whose conductor difference is not polynomially smooth'
results.sec 6: Kohel's vertical-isogeny algorithm costs O(l^4); random reducibility across the whole class holds if c_pi is polynomially smooth; for Koblitz curves with CM by Q(sqrt(-7)) P(c_pi) is typically too large, 'we cannot prove random reducibility ... for all of the elliptic curves within the isogeny class'; the constructible curves are exactly the levels reachable from the top by Kohel's algorithm
results.Fig 1: NIST K-163..K-571 have large P(c_pi); ECC2K-130 is not in the table

JMV09.cite: D. Jao, S. D. Miller, R. Venkatesan, Expander graphs based on GRH with an application to elliptic curve cryptography, J. Number Theory 129 (2009) 1491-1504, arXiv 0811.0647

Kohel96.cite: D. Kohel, Endomorphism rings of elliptic curves over finite fields, PhD thesis, UC Berkeley, 1996

results.Prop 21: prime-degree l isogeny: one endomorphism ring contains the other with index dividing l
results.Prop 22: End(E) = End(E') iff there is an isogeny E->E' of degree prime to deg(phi) (via Tate modules)
results.Prop 23: (D/l)+1 horizontal l-isogenies when O is maximal at l; none if not; descending count l-(D/l) (up to unit index)
results.Thm 1 = Thm 24: End(E) computable deterministically in O(q^(1/3+eps)) under a GRH
results.Lemma 25: kernel of pi - a on E[n] in O(n^2 log n log q) (needs division polynomial of degree ~n^2)

Sut13.cite: A. V. Sutherland, Isogeny volcanoes, ANTS X (2012), Open Book Series 1 (2013) 507-530, arXiv 1208.5370

results.Thm 7 (Kohel): ordinary components of the l-isogeny graph are l-volcanoes; depth = v_l of the conductor of Z[pi] over that of the crater
results.Remark 5: horizontal isogenies decompose into small-degree ones via class-group relations (subexponential under GRH); vertical ones do not
results.sec 3.3: 'we do not know any algorithm for computing a vertical l-isogeny whose complexity is not at least linear in l (in general, quadratic in l)'; Example 13: kernel element of a large-prime vertical isogeny needs > 2^80 bits

Gal99.cite: S. D. Galbraith, Constructing isogenies between elliptic curves over finite fields, LMS J. Comput. Math. 2 (1999) 118-138

results.Thm 1: RH for imaginary quadratic fields: isogeny construction in expected worst-case O(p^(3/2) ln p)
results.sec 6: if the conductor is O(ln p)-smooth: expected O(p^(1/4) (ln p)^(13/2)); polynomial if h is polylog
results.Prop 1: if l divides the index of the endomorphism rings then deg(phi) is divisible by l (Kohel Prop 21)
results.sec 2: 'main exception': End(E1) in End(E2) with index divisible by a large prime - 'it is not clear what the relationship is between the difficulty of the discrete logarithm problems'
results.sec 8: if one conductor is divisible by the large prime and the other is not, 'there is no shortcut available'

GHS02.cite: S. D. Galbraith, F. Hess, N. P. Smart, Extending the GHS Weil descent attack, EUROCRYPT 2002, LNCS 2332, pp. 29-44 (ePrint 2001/054)

results.Thm 3: Galbraith's isogeny algorithm: worst case O(q^(3n/2+eps)), average O(q^(n/4+eps)) operations in F_(q^n)
results.sec 3: low-memory random-walk version, expected average O(q^(n/4+eps)); 'Stage 0' (ascending to the maximal order) is the worst-case bottleneck when the square part of Delta has a large prime factor; a smooth ideal representation makes the found isogeny evaluable in polynomial time
results.Thm 2 (= Menezes-Qu): n odd prime, t = ord_n(2): the smallest attainable GHS magic number m > 1 is t+1
results.scope: extended (isogeny-walk) GHS attack works only for fields of composite degree over F_2

results.Thm 4.2: End(E) of an ordinary E/F_q determined in polynomial time O(log^(7+2u) q) given the factorisation of Delta_pi (tests whether (pi-a)/g is an endomorphism via the embedding lemma) - so the LEVEL of any curve is identifiable in polynomial time
